main.title: A 45,000-person labor strike at Samsung's memory chip plants could throw a wrench into the AI boom
main.body:
Samsung's unionized workers plan a historic 18-day work stoppage beginning May 21, representing the largest semiconductor industry strike ever. This action threatens a critical chokepoint in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Samsung manufactures approximately one-third of global DRAM and controls roughly two-thirds of the DRAM market alongside SK Hynix. The two companies dominate high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the specialized chips essential for AI systems.

Workers seek 15% of annual operating profit for bonuses, removal of bonus caps currently limited to 50% of base salary, and a 7% wage increase. Management countered with 13% of operating profit as a one-time 2026 payment, refusing permanent structural changes.

SK Hynix recently settled with its union on 10% annual profit allocation — currently paying workers approximately $460,000–$477,000 annually. Samsung employees have been departing to SK Hynix, with roughly 200 transfers occurring over four months.

An April test strike reduced foundry output 58% and memory fabrication 18% during a single shift. Industry estimates project potential losses between 30–100 trillion won if the full strike proceeds.

Samsung struggles competing in high-bandwidth memory markets against SK Hynix and Micron. A prolonged disruption could undermine recovery efforts, as the company's newly developed HBM4 chips have exceeded expectations with 2026 production already fully sold out.
main.keep_reason: Samsung 5/21 18일 총파업이 HBM 공급망과 글로벌 AI 인프라에 직격 — 한국 반도체 산업 최대 사건이자 시장 동향 핵심.
main.select_reason: 5/21 18일 총파업이 HBM4 100% 매진 상태에서 발생 — 글로벌 AI 인프라 직격, 30~100조원 손실 추정. 정의적 한국 반도체 사건.

main.title: NVIDIA prepares shipment of 82,000 AI GPUs to China as chip war lines blur — H200 shipments with 25% tax to begin as US loosens restrictions
main.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang confirmed during Beijing summit proceedings that the company has received export licenses for multiple Chinese customers, has purchase orders in hand, and has restarted H200 manufacturing, marking a significant development in the stalled trade negotiations.

Approved Buyers: Around 10 Chinese companies including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and JD.com are cleared by the U.S. Commerce Department to purchase Nvidia's H200 chips, along with distributors like Lenovo and Foxconn.

Export Framework: The U.S. arrangement requires a 25% revenue share payment to the U.S. Treasury on each sale, inter-agency approval for individual transactions. Restrictions remain on newer Blackwell and Rubin architectures.

Current Status: Despite U.S. approval, deals have stalled because China instructed domestic companies to limit Nvidia chip purchases. President Trump stated China 'chose not to' approve purchases because 'they want to develop their own.' Nvidia's market share in China has collapsed from approximately 95% to near zero.

Jensen Huang's Stanford Statement (May 17, 2026): Huang slammed the nuclear weapons analogy for GPU export controls, calling it 'stupid.' He said US policy has 'already largely backfired' and Nvidia has 'zero percent' market share in China. He advocates allowing GPU sales to adversarial countries.
main.keep_reason: 엔비디아 H200 중국 수출 라이선스+25% 세금 부과 구조 확정 — 글로벌 GPU 공급망 재편의 구체적 진전.
main.select_reason: H200 수출 재개 + Treasury 25% 매출 분배라는 신규 정책 프레임워크 + Alibaba/Tencent/ByteDance 등 구체적 승인 — 수출통제 신모델 정립.

main.title: SK Hynix Locks Up 2026 HBM Capacity and Snares 200 Samsung Engineers in AI Memory Blitz
main.body:
South Korean memory manufacturer SK Hynix has achieved significant milestones. The company has sold out all 2026 HBM capacity and simultaneously recruited approximately 200 engineers from Samsung within a four-month period. The stock has experienced dramatic appreciation, climbing nearly 169% since the beginning of the year.

Financial Performance: First quarter 2026 sales reached 52.6 trillion Won with operating profit of 37.6 trillion Won, representing a 72% margin. Operating profit projections for the full year stand at approximately 277 trillion Won.

Competitive Advantages: The extreme scarcity of AI memory components has strengthened the company's negotiating position. Customers are being locked into multiyear supply contracts featuring upfront payments and shared development investments.

Talent Acquisition Strategy: Since September, the company has directed 10% of annual operating profit toward an uncapped performance bonus pool, making it an attractive employer relative to competitors facing labor disputes.

Market Outlook: Nomura Securities projects demand for specialized AI memory will increase 'a thousandfold over the next five years,' while supply expands at only 30% annually, maintaining favorable pricing dynamics for the producer.

main.title: US FTC reportedly launches antitrust probe into Arm following its launch of its own AGI CPU — regulators investigate if chip designer is restricting architecture access to rivals
main.body:
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has reportedly initiated an antitrust investigation into Arm Holdings, examining whether the chip architecture designer is leveraging its market position to restrict competitors' access to its technology. This probe follows Arm's March 2026 launch of its own AGI data center processor, marking a significant business shift from its traditional licensing-only model.

The investigation centers on concerns that Arm may be offering inferior designs to licensing customers or denying them access altogether. Industry observers worry that Arm's entry into actual chip manufacturing could unfairly advantage its own products while disadvantaging the companies that depend on its architecture licenses.

The regulatory scrutiny stems partly from Arm's 2023 lawsuit against Qualcomm regarding Nuvia acquisition licensing rights — a case Arm lost. Qualcomm subsequently launched a global antitrust campaign against Arm, filing complaints with regulators in Europe, the U.S., and South Korea. South Korea's Fair Trade Commission raided Arm's Seoul office in November 2025.

The stakes are significant: Arm architecture dominates mobile processors and is expected to power over 90% of custom AI server processors by 2029, according to analyst projections. Major licensees including Apple, Qualcomm, Samsung, and MediaTek now face potential competitive disadvantages as their former partner becomes a direct competitor.
main.keep_reason: Arm의 자체 AGI CPU 진출에 따른 FTC 반독점 조사 — 2029년 AI 서버 CPU 90% 점유 예상 회사의 사업 모델 전환과 직결.
main.select_reason: 2029년 AI 서버 CPU 90% 점유 예상 Arm의 FTC 반독점 조사 — Apple/Qualcomm/Samsung 라이선시 직접 영향, 미·EU·韓 동시 조사.

main.title: Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon capex spending to hit $725 billion in 2026, up 77% from last year — analyst says bear thesis is 'garbage'
main.body:
The four major technology companies plan unprecedented infrastructure investments driven by artificial intelligence development. Combined capex spending will reach $725 billion in 2026, representing a dramatic 77% increase compared to 2025's $410 billion.

Individual Company Spending: Microsoft: $190 billion (significantly above the $152 billion analyst average); Alphabet/Google: Up to $190 billion; Meta: $145 billion (increased by $10 billion from previous guidance); Amazon: approximately $200 billion.

Primary Drivers: Rising memory chip and component costs significantly impact forecasts. Microsoft's CFO Amy Hood attributed '$25 billion of that figure to rising memory chip and component costs.' Meta similarly cited 'higher component pricing, particularly for memory' alongside increased expenses for land, power, and skilled workers.

Market Performance & Justification: Analyst sentiment supports these investments. One analyst characterized skepticism as 'garbage,' arguing the AI economy demonstrates health through revenue growth. Google Cloud achieved impressive results, with quarterly revenue reaching $20 billion and a contract backlog of $460 billion.

Despite massive spending, companies remain capacity-constrained as they race to deploy infrastructure faster than competitors.

Note: While the article was published April 30, 2026, it was first linked and cited widely in the May 16-18 weekend tech review cycle as ongoing context for datacenter buildout. Publication date confirmed April 30, 2026 — included as a contextual background article for this issue.

main.title: AI data centers trigger massive 'irreversible' 76% electricity price spike in largest US region — federal watchdog demands tech giants pay for their own power infrastructure
main.body:
Monitoring Analytics, the federal watchdog overseeing the PJM Interconnection — the largest power distribution region in the U.S. — released a report documenting a dramatic surge in electricity costs driven by AI data center demand. Wholesale power prices jumped from $77.78 per megawatt-hour in Q1 2025 to $136.53 per megawatt-hour in Q1 2026, representing a 75.5% increase.

The watchdog stated that 'The price impacts on customers have been very large and are not reversible,' warning that costs will worsen unless data center load issues are resolved before the June 2026 capacity auction.

The Core Issue: PJM is incorporating massive data center demands into its standard capacity forecasting process, which inflates wholesale prices for all electricity consumers, including households and small businesses.

Proposed Solution: The report recommends requiring data centers to negotiate directly with power producers rather than participating in the general auction, ensuring these large consumers bear the infrastructure costs rather than spreading expenses across all ratepayers.

The article notes growing federal scrutiny, including Trump administration pressure on tech giants to develop their own power generation infrastructure.

main.select_reason: PJM Q1 가격 75.5% 급등($77.78→$136.53/MWh) — '비가역적' 명시 — DPU/효율 솔루션의 TCO 가치 명제와 직결.

main.title: 김민석 총리 "삼성전자 파업하면 긴급조정 등 모든 수단 강구"
main.body:
김민석 국무총리가 노사가 합의에 이르지 못할 경우 긴급조정을 시행하겠다는 공개 성명을 발표했다. 그는 '파업으로 국가 경제에 막대한 피해가 우려되는 상황이 발생한다면 정부는 긴급조정을 포함한 모든 가능한 대응 수단을 강구하지 않을 수 없다'고 밝혔다.

노사는 5월 18일 오전 10시경 세종 중앙노동위원회에서 두 번째 사후조정 회의를 개최할 예정이었다. 총리는 이것이 파업을 막기 위한 마지막 기회임을 강조하며 양측이 이를 가볍게 여기지 않도록 촉구했다.

배경: 이전 협상(5월 11~13일)은 성과급 지급 기준에 대한 불일치로 실패했다. 그 이후 삼성 18명의 이사들의 사과와 이재용 회장의 사과를 포함한 여러 화해 시도가 이루어졌다.

긴급 조정 절차는 1963년 도입 이후 4번만 사용된 것으로, 30일간 즉시 파업을 중단하고 강제 조정 및 중재가 진행된다.
main.keep_reason: 김민석 총리 긴급조정 발동 시사 — 1963년 이후 4번뿐인 강제 조정 절차 가능성 — 정부 개입 강도.
main.select_reason: Samsung 파업 saga 보완 — 1963년 이후 4번뿐인 긴급조정 절차 가능성 명시, 정부 개입 수위 본격 격상.

main.title: ST, 엔비디아 AI 데이터센터 '800V' 전력설계 겨냥…"시장 수요에 적기 대응"
main.body:
STMicroelectronics가 차세대 AI 데이터센터를 위한 NVIDIA의 800 VDC(볼트 직류) 전력 아키텍처를 지원할 준비가 됐다고 발표했다. 아시아-태평양 마케팅 및 영업 담당 수석 부사장 히로시 노구치는 회사가 탄화규소(SiC), 질화갈륨(GaN), 디지털 전력 설계 역량을 포함한 핵심 기술을 보유하고 있다고 밝혔다.

800 VDC 접근 방식은 급증하는 데이터센터 전력 수요를 해결한다. 국제에너지기구(IEA)는 데이터센터 전력 소비가 2030년까지 945 테라와트시를 초과할 것으로 예측하며, 이는 2024년 수준의 두 배 이상이자 한국의 연간 소비량을 넘는 수치다.

기술 작동 방식: 서버 랙에 800V를 직접 공급함으로써 전압 변환 단계를 줄이고 에너지 손실을 최소화한다. ST는 800V를 50V, 12V, 6V로 변환하는 솔루션을 개발했다. GaN 기반 부품은 2600W/in³ 전력 밀도에서 98% 효율을 달성한다.

NVIDIA는 800 VDC 아키텍처가 2027년 카버(Kaber) 랙 스케일 시스템의 상업적 배포와 함께 본격 채택될 것으로 기대하고 있다.
main.keep_reason: NVIDIA Kyber 2027 랙 + 800VDC 아키텍처 — AI 데이터센터 전력 효율 핵심 과제와 ST의 SiC/GaN 솔루션.
main.select_reason: NVIDIA Kyber 2027 랙용 800VDC 아키텍처 + ST SiC/GaN 솔루션 — DPU 인접 데이터센터 전력 아키텍처 전환 신호.

main.title: 삼성·SK하이닉스, 1분기 연구개발비 최대 68% 급증
main.body:
삼성전자의 1분기 R&D 비용은 11조 3000억 원으로 전년 동기 9조 원 대비 '25.5% 증가'를 기록했다. 회사는 AI 반도체 발전에 초점을 맞춰 2026년에 '시설 및 R&D 투자 110조 원 이상을 집행'할 계획이다.

SK하이닉스의 1분기 R&D 지출은 2조 5500억 원으로 전년 동기 1조 5100억 원 대비 약 '68.3% 증가'를 기록했다. 인건비가 총 지출의 가장 큰 비중을 차지했으며 1조 3500억 원에 달했다.

주요 개발 초점: 두 회사 모두 HBM4E(6세대 고대역폭 메모리) 개발에 적극적으로 나서고 있다. 삼성은 2026년 2분기 샘플 출하를 계획하고 있으며, SK하이닉스는 2026년 하반기를 목표로 하고 있으며, 양산은 2027년에 예정되어 있다. AI 메모리 칩 개발의 경쟁 강도가 이러한 상당한 R&D 투자의 주요 동력으로 파악된다.
main.keep_reason: 삼성/SK하이닉스 1Q R&D 25.5%/68.3% 증가, HBM4E 6세대 개발 가속 — 메모리 경쟁의 강도 측정 지표.
main.select_reason: 삼성 25.5% / SK 68.3% R&D 급증 + HBM4E 6세대 로드맵(삼성 2Q'26 샘플, SK 2H'26) — 메모리 경쟁 강도 정량지표.

main.title: $60B AI chip darling Cerebras almost died early on, burning $8M a month
main.body:
Cerebras Systems recently completed what was 2026's largest tech IPO, achieving a $60 billion valuation. However, the company nearly failed years earlier while attempting an unprecedented engineering challenge.

In 2019, the AI chip startup faced an existential crisis while trying to solve a 'packaging' problem that had stumped the semiconductor industry for decades. The company was hemorrhaging approximately $8 million monthly and had already consumed nearly $200 million in capital.

The core innovation involved creating a single massive wafer-sized chip rather than connecting multiple smaller processors. This approach required solving unprecedented cooling, power delivery, and data management issues. According to founder Andrew Feldman: 'We destroyed an enormous number of chips' during trial-and-error testing.

The breakthrough came in July 2019 when the team successfully powered on a fully packaged chip. Feldman described the moment: the founding team 'just stood in the lab and stared at it,' overwhelmed by achieving what the industry deemed impossible.

Today, Cerebras supplies AI inference chips to major customers including OpenAI and AWS, with OpenAI holding significant equity stakes through a $1 billion loan arrangement. The company's wafer-scale engine is 58 times bigger than Nvidia's B200 chip and provides substantially greater memory bandwidth.
main.keep_reason: Cerebras IPO 후 600억 달러 기업가치 달성 — 웨이퍼 스케일 엔진의 B200 대비 58배 크기 등 AI 추론 가속기 경쟁사 동향.
main.select_reason: $60B 기업가치 IPO 완료 — 웨이퍼 스케일 엔진(B200 58배) AI 추론 가속기 경쟁사의 자본시장 진입 마일스톤.

main.title: Huawei could seize China's AI chip crown in 2026 as Nvidia's H200 shipments stall in regulatory limbo
main.body:
Huawei is positioned to dominate China's artificial intelligence chip market in 2026. This shift is driven by regulatory constraints limiting Nvidia's H200 chip shipments into the Chinese market and Beijing's active push for domestic semiconductor champions.

As of May 2026, Nvidia can sell its H200 chip to China under the Trump administration's December policy reversal, but not a single delivery has been made. Chinese tech companies pulled back after Beijing instructed them to limit use of Nvidia chips to overseas operations, prioritizing Huawei's Ascend chips domestically.

The China AI chip market is projected to hit $67 billion by 2030. Huawei has braced for approximately $12 billion in AI chip revenue driven by homegrown AI model demand.

Huawei's Ascend chips are manufactured by SMIC (Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation), China's leading fab. The chips are seen as competitive for many AI workloads, though still behind NVIDIA's H100/H200 in raw performance.

Jensen Huang's attendance at the Trump-Xi summit (May 13–15) raised hopes of unlocking the market, but China's position has not meaningfully shifted as of mid-May.
main.keep_reason: Huawei Ascend SMIC 양산 + 670억 달러 중국 AI 칩 시장 — 글로벌 GPU 경쟁구도의 양극화 진전.
main.select_reason: Huawei Ascend $12B 매출 전망 + $67B 중국 AI 칩 시장 — H200 정체와 짝지어 글로벌 GPU 경쟁 양극화의 대척점 데이터.

main.title: 엔비디아, 'RTX 5090' 한장으로 1분 영상 생성하는 월드 모델 오픈 공개
main.body:
엔비디아가 26억 개의 파라미터를 갖춘 오픈소스 월드 모델인 SANA-WM을 공개했다. 이 시스템은 단 하나의 RTX 5090으로 34초 만에 720p 제어 가능한 영상 60초를 생성할 수 있다.

이 모델은 단일 GPU에서 작동하며, 이전에 경쟁사들이 여러 GPU를 필요로 했던 한계를 해결한다. 212,975개의 비디오 클립으로 학습되었으며 하이브리드 선형 어텐션 아키텍처, 이중 분기 카메라 제어, 2단계 생성 정제, 6-DOF 카메라 데이터에 대한 자동화된 주석 파이프라인의 네 가지 핵심 기술을 포함한다.

엔비디아는 약 15일 동안 64개의 H100 GPU를 사용해 SANA-WM을 훈련시켰다. 성능 벤치마크에서 720p 해상도에서 'VBench Overall' 점수가 80점대를 달성했으며 경쟁 모델보다 최대 36배 높은 처리량을 보여줬다.

모델 코드는 GitHub에서 사용 가능하며 곧 가중치도 공개될 예정이다.
main.keep_reason: NVIDIA SANA-WM 오픈소스 — RTX 5090 1장으로 720p 60초 영상 생성, 단일 GPU 효율 36배 향상 — AI 모델 최적화 핵심.
main.select_reason: SANA-WM 오픈소스 — RTX 5090 단일 GPU 720p 60초 생성, 경쟁모델 대비 처리량 36배 — AI 모델 효율화 흐름의 구체 진전.

competitor_articles.title: US FTC reportedly launches antitrust probe into Arm following its launch of its own AGI CPU — regulators investigate if chip designer is restricting architecture access to rivals
competitor_articles.body:
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has reportedly initiated an antitrust investigation into Arm Holdings, examining whether the chip architecture designer is leveraging its market position to restrict competitors' access to its technology. This probe follows Arm's March 2026 launch of its own AGI data center processor, marking a significant business shift from its traditional licensing-only model.

The investigation centers on concerns that Arm may be offering inferior designs to licensing customers or denying them access altogether. Industry observers worry that Arm's entry into actual chip manufacturing could unfairly advantage its own products while disadvantaging the companies that depend on its architecture licenses.

The regulatory scrutiny stems partly from Arm's 2023 lawsuit against Qualcomm regarding Nuvia acquisition licensing rights — a case Arm lost. Qualcomm subsequently launched a global antitrust campaign against Arm, filing complaints with regulators in Europe, the U.S., and South Korea. South Korea's Fair Trade Commission raided Arm's Seoul office in November 2025.

The stakes are significant: Arm architecture dominates mobile processors and is expected to power over 90% of custom AI server processors by 2029, according to analyst projections. Major licensees including Apple, Qualcomm, Samsung, and MediaTek now face potential competitive disadvantages as their former partner becomes a direct competitor.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: Arm의 자체 AGI CPU 진출에 따른 FTC 반독점 조사 — 2029년 AI 서버 CPU 90% 점유 예상 회사의 사업 모델 전환과 직결.

competitor_articles.title: $60B AI chip darling Cerebras almost died early on, burning $8M a month
competitor_articles.body:
Cerebras Systems recently completed what was 2026's largest tech IPO, achieving a $60 billion valuation. However, the company nearly failed years earlier while attempting an unprecedented engineering challenge.

In 2019, the AI chip startup faced an existential crisis while trying to solve a 'packaging' problem that had stumped the semiconductor industry for decades. The company was hemorrhaging approximately $8 million monthly and had already consumed nearly $200 million in capital.

The core innovation involved creating a single massive wafer-sized chip rather than connecting multiple smaller processors. This approach required solving unprecedented cooling, power delivery, and data management issues. According to founder Andrew Feldman: 'We destroyed an enormous number of chips' during trial-and-error testing.

The breakthrough came in July 2019 when the team successfully powered on a fully packaged chip. Feldman described the moment: the founding team 'just stood in the lab and stared at it,' overwhelmed by achieving what the industry deemed impossible.

Today, Cerebras supplies AI inference chips to major customers including OpenAI and AWS, with OpenAI holding significant equity stakes through a $1 billion loan arrangement. The company's wafer-scale engine is 58 times bigger than Nvidia's B200 chip and provides substantially greater memory bandwidth.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: Cerebras IPO 후 600억 달러 기업가치 달성 — 웨이퍼 스케일 엔진의 B200 대비 58배 크기 등 AI 추론 가속기 경쟁사 동향.

competitor_articles.title: Huawei could seize China's AI chip crown in 2026 as Nvidia's H200 shipments stall in regulatory limbo
competitor_articles.body:
Huawei is positioned to dominate China's artificial intelligence chip market in 2026. This shift is driven by regulatory constraints limiting Nvidia's H200 chip shipments into the Chinese market and Beijing's active push for domestic semiconductor champions.

As of May 2026, Nvidia can sell its H200 chip to China under the Trump administration's December policy reversal, but not a single delivery has been made. Chinese tech companies pulled back after Beijing instructed them to limit use of Nvidia chips to overseas operations, prioritizing Huawei's Ascend chips domestically.

The China AI chip market is projected to hit $67 billion by 2030. Huawei has braced for approximately $12 billion in AI chip revenue driven by homegrown AI model demand.

Huawei's Ascend chips are manufactured by SMIC (Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation), China's leading fab. The chips are seen as competitive for many AI workloads, though still behind NVIDIA's H100/H200 in raw performance.

Jensen Huang's attendance at the Trump-Xi summit (May 13–15) raised hopes of unlocking the market, but China's position has not meaningfully shifted as of mid-May.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: Huawei Ascend SMIC 양산 + 670억 달러 중국 AI 칩 시장 — 글로벌 GPU 경쟁구도의 양극화 진전.

competitor_articles.title: Jensen Huang slams 'stupid' analogy comparing GPUs to nuclear weapons — Nvidia CEO says government should allow selling GPUs to adversarial countries
competitor_articles.body:
During a Stanford University guest lecture, Nvidia's CEO rejected comparisons between AI chip exports and nuclear weapons proliferation. Huang criticized Anthropic leader Dario Amodei's analogy equating GPU sales to adversarial nations with providing nuclear weapons to hostile regimes.

Huang's core argument: 'There are a billion people with Nvidia GPUs...but I don't advocate atomic bombs to anybody.' He characterized the comparison as fundamentally flawed reasoning that prevents constructive policy discussion.

The CEO has consistently opposed U.S. export controls on AI processors, previously stating such restrictions have 'backfired' and resulted in Nvidia losing market share in China. His position reflects frustration with policies limiting advanced semiconductor access to certain countries.

The article highlights the broader tension between national security concerns and industry leaders who believe restrictions ultimately disadvantage American companies while driving international competitors to develop alternatives.

Context: Despite Trump administration approving H200 exports to around 10 Chinese firms, China has blocked domestic purchases — instructing companies to prioritize Huawei and domestic chips. Huang's $78 billion Q1 FY2027 guidance assumes zero H200 recovery from China.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: 젠슨 황 스탠퍼드 연설 — 수출 통제 정책 비판, 78B Q1 가이던스 컨텍스트 — NVIDIA 리더십 시각 직접 청취.

competitor_articles.title: ST, 엔비디아 AI 데이터센터 '800V' 전력설계 겨냥…"시장 수요에 적기 대응"
competitor_articles.body:
STMicroelectronics가 차세대 AI 데이터센터를 위한 NVIDIA의 800 VDC(볼트 직류) 전력 아키텍처를 지원할 준비가 됐다고 발표했다. 아시아-태평양 마케팅 및 영업 담당 수석 부사장 히로시 노구치는 회사가 탄화규소(SiC), 질화갈륨(GaN), 디지털 전력 설계 역량을 포함한 핵심 기술을 보유하고 있다고 밝혔다.

800 VDC 접근 방식은 급증하는 데이터센터 전력 수요를 해결한다. 국제에너지기구(IEA)는 데이터센터 전력 소비가 2030년까지 945 테라와트시를 초과할 것으로 예측하며, 이는 2024년 수준의 두 배 이상이자 한국의 연간 소비량을 넘는 수치다.

기술 작동 방식: 서버 랙에 800V를 직접 공급함으로써 전압 변환 단계를 줄이고 에너지 손실을 최소화한다. ST는 800V를 50V, 12V, 6V로 변환하는 솔루션을 개발했다. GaN 기반 부품은 2600W/in³ 전력 밀도에서 98% 효율을 달성한다.

NVIDIA는 800 VDC 아키텍처가 2027년 카버(Kaber) 랙 스케일 시스템의 상업적 배포와 함께 본격 채택될 것으로 기대하고 있다.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: NVIDIA Kyber 2027 랙 + 800VDC 아키텍처 — AI 데이터센터 전력 효율 핵심 과제와 ST의 SiC/GaN 솔루션.

competitor_articles.title: 엔비디아, 'RTX 5090' 한장으로 1분 영상 생성하는 월드 모델 오픈 공개
competitor_articles.body:
엔비디아가 26억 개의 파라미터를 갖춘 오픈소스 월드 모델인 SANA-WM을 공개했다. 이 시스템은 단 하나의 RTX 5090으로 34초 만에 720p 제어 가능한 영상 60초를 생성할 수 있다.

이 모델은 단일 GPU에서 작동하며, 이전에 경쟁사들이 여러 GPU를 필요로 했던 한계를 해결한다. 212,975개의 비디오 클립으로 학습되었으며 하이브리드 선형 어텐션 아키텍처, 이중 분기 카메라 제어, 2단계 생성 정제, 6-DOF 카메라 데이터에 대한 자동화된 주석 파이프라인의 네 가지 핵심 기술을 포함한다.

엔비디아는 약 15일 동안 64개의 H100 GPU를 사용해 SANA-WM을 훈련시켰다. 성능 벤치마크에서 720p 해상도에서 'VBench Overall' 점수가 80점대를 달성했으며 경쟁 모델보다 최대 36배 높은 처리량을 보여줬다.

모델 코드는 GitHub에서 사용 가능하며 곧 가중치도 공개될 예정이다.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: NVIDIA SANA-WM 오픈소스 — RTX 5090 1장으로 720p 60초 영상 생성, 단일 GPU 효율 36배 향상 — AI 모델 최적화 핵심.

competitor_articles.title: 미 FTC, '직접 칩 설계' 나선 Arm 반독점 조사 착수
competitor_articles.body:
미국 연방거래위원회(FTC)가 ARM 홀딩스에 대한 반독점 조사에 착수했으며, 반도체 설계 회사가 직접 칩 제조로 사업을 확장하면서 경쟁업체의 기술 라이선스 접근을 제한하고 있는지 조사하고 있다.

Bloomberg에 따르면 FTC는 Arm이 직접 칩을 개발하면서 다른 기업들의 CPU 설계 라이선스 품질을 저하하거나 접근을 제한하는지 여부를 조사하고 있다. 기관은 올해 초 Arm에 조사를 통보하고 관련 문서 보존을 요청했다.

주요 포인트: Arm은 전통적으로 직접 칩을 제조하기보다는 CPU 설계와 명령어 세트 아키텍처(ISA)를 라이선스했다. 회사는 3월에 자체 칩 사업을 확장할 계획을 발표했으며, 업계 예측에 따르면 5년 내 연간 150억 달러의 수익을 창출할 수 있다. 퀄컴은 Arm이 시장 지배력을 이용해 경쟁업체의 접근을 제한한다고 주장했다. 유럽위원회와 한국 공정거래위원회도 Arm의 관행을 조사하고 있다.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: Arm FTC 반독점 조사 한국어 1차 정리본 — 한국 공정위 수원 사무소 압수수색 등 한국 맥락 추가.
